UT-2026-SB254.policyArea: Administrative Rulemaking and Procedures, Income Tax, Mining
UT-2026-SB254.aiSummary: This law sets up new rules for critical minerals projects in Utah. It would speed up some state permit reviews, create a Critical Minerals Council, and set up a Critical Minerals Atlas, a data clearinghouse, and a development account. It also changes property tax rules for critical minerals zones and sets aside $11 million for fiscal year 2027.

UT-2026-HB457.aiSummary: The law changes some county and annexation rules in Utah. It requires certain unincorporated islands in second-class counties to automatically join a nearby city or town, unless a local law body exempts them, and it changes notice rules for those annexations. It also lets some counties use non-contiguous areas on a final annexation plat and update how a county under a council-manager system can delegate accounting work.

UT-2026-HB103.policyArea: Crimes, Fraud, Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice
UT-2026-HB103.aiSummary: The law sets new crimes for marrying a minor, helping move a minor out of state for an illegal marriage, and traveling out of state to marry a minor. It also makes it a crime for a parent or guardian to allow an illegal marriage, for someone to falsely act as a parent or guardian, and for a person to officiate a minor's marriage when it does not meet Utah's rules. It adds a 15-year time limit to bring cases for the new marriage crimes and says some out-of-state marriages involving a minor are not valid in Utah unless they meet certain rules. The bill became law on March 26, 2026.

UT-2026-SB98.policyArea: Administrative Rulemaking and Procedures, Appropriations, Department of Health and Human Services
UT-2026-SB98.aiSummary: The bill lets the health department create a program that can certify employers as a "recovery ready workplace," which means a workplace that meets state standards to support workers with substance use disorder. If the program is set up, the department would make the application process and rules, and it could use money from the state account that gets nicotine tax and penalty money. It also takes effect on May 6, 2026, and it was signed by the governor.

UT-2026-SB275.policyArea: Blockchain, Data and Cyber Security, Electronic Databases
UT-2026-SB275.aiSummary: This bill creates a state-run digital identity program in the Department of Government Operations. It sets rules for getting and using a state-endorsed digital identity, including using it as proof of age, and gives requirements for agencies, health care providers, wallet providers, and others that handle it. It also creates complaint and enforcement steps, orders a one-time audit, and the governor signed it on March 25, 2026.

UT-2026-HB247.policyArea: Great Salt Lake, Natural Resources, Revenue and Taxation
UT-2026-HB247.aiSummary: The bill became law and changes rules for Great Salt Lake taxes and money accounts. It shifts some brine shrimp tax money to the Sovereign Lands Management Account, changes tax rates and timing for some Great Salt Lake extraction operators, and sets how that account money may be spent. It also changes how some money from judgments or settlements tied to the lake is deposited and spent, and it keeps a reporting duty for the state on these funds.

UT-2026-HB187.aiSummary: Signed by the governor, this law changes some water rules for the lower basin of the Colorado River Compact. It exempts certain water rights held by a water conservancy district from abandonment or forfeiture rules, and it limits some change requests for instream flow water use. It also adds a coordination rule with another water bill and makes technical updates.
